title: Valkyrie (Anvil Aerospace, Star Citizen)

sources.title: Star Citizen game files: defaultProfile.xml and layout_t16000m_dual.xml (Data.p4k, build 4.8)

intro: The Valkyrie is a heavy dropship from Anvil Aerospace in Star Citizen, a ship that carries soldiers into a fight and lands them there. It has a two-seat cockpit and gunner stations, and its troop bay takes twenty soldiers and a vehicle. VTOL mode on left base button 5 matters for landing in a fight zone.

panels.name: Valkyrie: weapons and modules
panels.text: This lists the Valkyrie's own weapons and special equipment, as the MFD weapons page and the ship data show them.
panels.context: Everything else in this cockpit works as in every Star Citizen ship: the same visor HUD, screens, seat actions and two-stick layout.

controls.name: Pilot guns (two)
controls.text: The Valkyrie's pilot has two guns. The pilot aims them by pointing the ship's nose.
controls.context: The pilot fires them with the right stick's trigger in guns mode; the MFD weapons page shows their groups and how they aim.

controls.name: Cargo (90 SCU)
controls.text: The bay holds 90 SCU of cargo when it is not full of soldiers.
controls.context: Cargo is counted in SCU (standard cargo units, boxes of one fixed size). Traders fill the hold at stations and outposts.

areas.name: Crew stations
areas.text: The other seats and stations of the ship besides the pilot's.

panels.name: Valkyrie: crew stations
panels.text: These are the seats and stations of the Valkyrie besides the pilot's seat.
panels.context: Each crew member sits at a station of their own; the pilot flies while the others work turrets or other equipment.

controls.name: Co-pilot seat
controls.text: A second seat in the Valkyrie's cockpit beside the pilot. More people on board can share the work.
controls.context: A second person on board can take over jobs such as turrets, scanning or the radio, so the pilot can concentrate on flying.

controls.name: Turret stations
controls.text: Two manned and three remote turrets cover the place where the ship lands.
controls.context: A remote turret is aimed from a seat inside the ship through a camera, not from a glass bubble on the turret itself.

controls.name: Troop bay
controls.text: Seats for up to twenty soldiers and room for a ground vehicle.
controls.context: The pilot lands, the soldiers leave through the bay, and the turrets protect them while they get out.
